raw_response:
I am 53 years old and I have farmed these 8 mu in Quzhou County for 35 years. I only went to primary school, but I know my land better than any book. My family has five people — my wife and me, my son and his wife, and my grandson. My son works in a factory in Handan and sends money home, but the farm is still my responsibility. I learned everything by doing it and watching my neighbors. If I see Lao Zhang across the road getting good yield with something new, I will try it on one mu first.

Right now it is spring and my wheat is turning green. Last year I got about 920 jin per mu of wheat and about 1,100 jin per mu of maize. This year the dealer raised urea price by a few yuan per bag, but I am not cutting back. I would rather spend an extra 200 yuan on fertilizer than risk losing 500 jin of grain across my whole field. A bad harvest is a disaster; wasting some fertilizer is just money I could have saved.

For my wheat, I planted an improved variety called Jimai 22 last October after rotary tilling the field. I put down 80 jin per mu of compound fertilizer as base. Now I will topdress with 40 jin per mu of urea when the wheat greens up — that is two 50-kilogram bags of urea for my whole 8 mu. I will irrigate three times from my well: once now in March, once at jointing around April, and once when the grain is filling in May. Electricity for the pump costs about 30 yuan each time, but dry wheat gives shriveled grain. I will spray herbicide once, and then if I see aphids or disease I will spray one more time. I think I can get 920 jin per mu if the weather is normal.

For the summer maize, after I harvest wheat in early June I plant hybrid seed right away — probably Zhengdan 958, because that is what everyone in my village buys. It grows fast and gives heavy ears. I do not plow for maize anymore; five years ago the village technician told us no-till works fine after wheat harvest if you clear the straw, and I tried it and saw it was true. It saves me diesel and two days of labor. I put 60 jin per mu of compound fertilizer in the rows when I sow, and then at the big trumpet stage I topdress with 30 jin per mu of urea. I irrigate twice: once after sowing if the soil is dry, and once when the tassels come out. Two sprays — herbicide when the maize is small, and insecticide if the stem borers show up. I expect about 1,100 jin per mu.

I do the math on everything. A bag of urea is about 100 yuan now, compound fertilizer is 170 yuan per bag, and hybrid maize seed is 60 yuan per mu. My whole fertilizer bill for both crops will be about 2,500 yuan. But if I cut back by one bag and lose 50 jin per mu, that is 400 jin across 8 mu. At 1.2 yuan per jin, that is nearly 500 yuan lost just on wheat. So I apply a bit more, not less. I learned this by doing it, not from any school.
